About the Role

Biosphere has a technically ambitious roadmap with concrete milestones: new reactor technologies to de-risk and integrate into our demonstration plant. Your first job is to help us execute on these scoped challenges. You’ll own day-to-day R&D priorities, experimental decisions and delivery within agreed budgets. As you deliver, you’ll take increasing ownership of our highest-risk, highest-reward technical work, guided by our commercial priorities and commitments.

This is a management role. You’ll lead our small, multidisciplinary R&D team: setting priorities, coaching, reviewing data, and hiring as the work requires. You’ll bring a passion for rigorous experimental design, and prioritize projects backed by sound technoeconomic analysis. Everyone builds at a company our size, so expect to be hands-on too. This role will collaborate closely with our Principal Engineer and capital projects team. You’ll lead development and validation of the technologies assigned to your team, and together you’ll agree on requirements, acceptance criteria and the handoff into plant design and commissioning.

Responsibilities
- Lead and grow the R&D team
- Execute the milestones on our roadmap: take new reactor technologies and subsystems from proof of concept to validated designs, including pilot-scale reactors and next-generation reactor prototypes for our government-funded programs.
- Deliver validated designs and specifications for the 20,000-liter line, and support installation and commissioning.
- Lead the funded research projects assigned to you through delivery and technical reporting, working with project managers. Contribute to proposals when the work fits our priorities and capacity.
- Make process and techno-economic calls. For example: is it worth more to replace a specialty cleaning chemical with dilute commodity caustic, or to run our cleaning cycle at 65 °C instead of 80 °C?
- Set the standard for experimental design and statistics. For each test, decide what it must show, how many runs that takes and how to analyze it, including for rare events like contamination.
- Build the tools we use to track experiments and characterize failures.
- Run the portfolio of R&D efforts: give each program an owner, budget, milestones and a next decision; rank work by value, remaining cost and delivery risk; stop discretionary work that no longer justifies its cost, and escalate changes to contractual commitments.

What success looks like
- In your first 60 days, agree on a delivery plan for the R&D portfolio with the Biosphere management team: priorities, owners, milestone dates, acceptance criteria and dependencies with the plant team.
- The first technologies on our roadmap have validated designs, test data and acceptance criteria, and are built into the demonstration plant’s design.
- The funded research projects you lead meet their milestones and budgets without delaying our priority commitments.

What to know:

About the role

Every product Databricks ships has to be priced, contracted, rated and billed before it can earn a dollar. The Money organization builds the systems that make this happen, at hyperscaler scale and across every major cloud. We built the world's only cross-cloud integrated rating engine in-house, and it now rates billions of dollars in revenue. Our next goal is bigger: a fully automated, zero-touch order-to-cash flow where the platform is the source of truth for accounts, contracts and subscriptions, and Month End Close needs little or no human intervention.

In an era where the world is rapidly advancing towards a cleaner future through decarbonization, Energy Exemplar’s mission lies in ‘Empowering Transformative Energy Decisions’. Founded in 1999 in Adelaide, Australia, our award-winning software portfolio encompassing the modeling and simulation platform PLEXOS®, Aurora, and Adapt2, is trusted by innovative organizations across the globe. Through our technology and people, we strive to enable stakeholders from across the entire energy value chain to revolutionize the energy ecosystem and to collaboratively plan and execute for a sustainable energy future with unprecedented clarity, speed, and innovation.

Our impact is global and is being recognized across the industry. Some of our recent accolades include:
- SaaS Company of the Year (2025) – Global Business Tech Awards.

Utilities, ISOs/RTOs, developers, and regulators look to the Director for how Energy Exemplar's platform and AI agents run securely and at scale alongside their own cloud estates. About Us: EvolutionIQ’s mission is to deliver state of the art technology that helps insurance claims teams make claims handling more accurate, fair, and efficient, so that more people impacted by injury or illness can continue their lives with dignity and stability. We are currently experiencing massive growth and to accomplish our goals, we are hiring world-class talent who want to help build and scale internally, and transform the insurance space. Our team is our #1 priority, and we have been named one of Inc.’s Best Workplaces 3 years in a row and Built In’s Best Places to work in 2025 and 2026!

As the Director, Data Insights, you will be the primary bridge between our technical depth and our most critical business decisions. You aren't just managing data; you are managing influence . Your mission is to translate complex data signals into persuasive business narratives that change how our internal leaders and external partners operate.

Key Responsibilities:
- Executive Advisory: Serve as the "Data Voice" in the room for high-stakes meetings with C-suite executives and external stakeholders. You will defend findings, negotiate priorities, and provide real-time strategic counsel.
- Narrative Design: Take the raw output from our data science and engineering teams and synthesize it into "Board-ready" presentations that drive multi-million dollar decisions.
- Culture Transformation: Act as a change agent to move the organization from "data-aware" to "data-driven." You will challenge existing business assumptions and push for evidence-based pivots.
- Stakeholder Diplomacy: Navigate conflicting interests between departments (e.g., Sales vs. Product) by using data as the objective "source of truth" to build consensus.
- Value Realization: Work closely with the data team to ensure their technical roadmap is strictly aligned with the highest-value business outcomes.

Qualifications:
- Strategic Pedigree: Proven experience leading high-level discussions with internal and external stakeholders.
- Data Fluency: While you may not be coding daily, you have a deep understanding of data science workflows, analytics engineering, and statistical significance.
- Communication Mastery: Exceptional ability to visualize data and craft compelling slide decks or memos for executive audiences.
- Business Acumen: A deep understanding of how businesses make money and how data can be used to optimize those levers.
- A Modern Day Individual Contribitor:  Can leverage agentic tools to do quick analytics as needed for high pressure leadership discussions.

Work-life, Culture & Perks:
- Compensation: The base salary range is $250-280K, with flexibility depending on a candidate’s background and experience. An annual bonus plan and company equity plan (RSUs) are also included in our compensation package.
- Well-Being: Medical, dental, vision, short & long-term disability, life insurance and AD&D, and 401k matching. Additional family, wellness, and pet benefits.

Fivetran and dbt Labs are bringing together two industry-leading companies with a shared mission: helping organizations unlock the full value of their data.

Flex is a growth-stage, NYC headquartered FinTech company that is building the payment layer for life's financial obligations, giving households one place to see, split, and pay their bills around how they live and get paid. By offering greater choice over how and when payments are made and allowing eligible on time payments to help build a positive credit history, Flex puts households back in control of their cash flow.

That work brings together people with different perspectives who challenge the status quo and take ownership of solving difficult problems. For you, that means doing the best work of your career next to people who make you better, and together bringing ideas to life that make a real impact for the people we serve.

We are seeking a strategic leader who pairs deep systems expertise with strong process design instincts to build and own Flex's Financial Systems & Transformation function from the ground up. This is a rare opportunity to define a new pillar within the Finance organization at a fast-scaling fintech — one where the scope extends well beyond traditional ERP administration into agentic AI infrastructure, process automation, and the controls architecture that will underpin Flex’s next phase of growth.

As Director, Financial Systems & Transformation, you will own the internal financial systems that power Flex’s accounting and financial reporting function — including our core ERP, procure-to-pay (P2P), T&E systems, and additional financial reporting tooling as the function matures. You will also design, build, and maintain the AI-powered workflows that are central to Flex’s vision for a modern, scalable Finance function, and you will lead the build-out of ITGC and financial systems controls that keep pace with the business as it scales.

This role sits at the intersection of finance, systems, and AI — and requires a leader who can operate with fluency across all three. You will partner closely with the VP Controller, the broader Finance leadership team, and Flex’s Engineering and AI Central teams to make the vision real. This position will be based in our New York headquarters on a hybrid basis and will report to the VP Controller.

Financial Systems Ownership & Administration
- Own our ERP (Campfire) as Flex’s financial system of record — including configuration, close module setup, chart of accounts and dimension/segment governance, and ongoing system health
- Own our procure-to-pay (P2P) systems for AP and T&E — evaluating near-term enhancements and long-term tooling strategy as we scale
- Manage integrations between core financial systems and the upstream/downstream data sources that feed them — including the payroll (Rippling) integration in partnership with the People/HRIS systems team — ensuring accurate, timely, and auditable data flows across the Finance stack

Judi Health is a health technology company providing benefit administration solutions to employers, unions, health plans, and government entities. Keyfactor is the leader in trust infrastructure for AI and machines, helping the world's largest enterprises and government agencies take control of the cryptographic identities that safeguard every digital interaction. Behind the platform is a global team of people who care deeply about the work and each other. We move fast, think big, and show up for one another every day. If you're looking for work that matters and a team that brings out your best, we hope you'll trust your future with Keyfactor!

- Define and articulate joint value propositions and go-to-market initiatives that drive new pipeline and revenue through GSI channels.

Enablement & Engagement
- Lead and/or facilitate efforts to  educate and enable  GSI teams (sales, technical, delivery) on Keyfactor solutions, positioning, and differentiation.

- Present Keyfactor’s value to senior executives and C-level leaders at partner and customer organizations.
- Collaborate internally, cross-functionally with Keyfactor’s regional sales, alliances, and marketing teams to drive alignment and joint execution globally,

Skills and Qualifications

About the Job:

LaunchDarkly is looking for a strategic, execution-oriented Director of Internal AI Operations to run and continuously improve how our company adopts and scales AI, establish the operational objectives, processes, and work plans that turn AI from a collection of tools into a measurable business capability and work with leaders across several functions to put the company’s AI direction into practice.

Responsibilities:
- Reporting: Build and maintain visibility into AI spend and usage. Develop adoption, efficiency, and cost metrics and report on tool overlap, cost drivers, and open risks. Support Finance with forecasting, budget tracking, anomaly detection, and vendor and model-cost optimization. Functional and technical leaders own efficiency, waste, cost, usage, and ROI within their portfolios; AI Operations prepares regular reporting and flags performance gaps for follow-up.
- Portfolio management: Maintain the inventory of AI tools, initiatives, agents, vendors, integrations, owners, status, spend, risks, and dependencies. Establish the processes and standards that keep it accurate across teams.
- Reviews: Participate in reviewing new AI Vendor requests and own and manage the Internal AI Feature Review process from intake through decision, conditions, approval, exception, or rejection, coordinating inputs from Security, Legal, IT, and business owners.
- Policy operations: Develop and maintain the company’s Internal AI Policy supporting resources with Legal and Security, and the Executive team, along with supporting resources. Recommend policy changes and put approved changes into operation.
- Transformation and migration: Track the AI roadmap, migrations, platform dependencies, adoption milestones, resourcing, risks, and executive decisions.
- Partnership with our technology teams : Collaborate on new AI product initiatives, empowering our product teams with how they identify and deliver value around AI.
- Administration and audit: Define and audit standards for access, ownership, configuration, data controls, logging, retention, vendor settings, and offboarding.
- Communications and enablement: Own the Internal AI communications calendar, stakeholder updates, FAQs, launch materials, training coordination, and policy-change communications.
- CoE coordination: Establish a common cadence and minimum artifacts across distributed AI CoEs without centralizing their technical or domain ownership.

Qualifications:
- 15+ years of progressively responsible experience in AI or technology operations, enterprise systems, data and analytics, FinOps, governance, transformation, or a related field, including 5+ years leading teams or complex cross-functional programs.
- Demonstrated success designing, implementing, or scaling an operating model across multiple functions, including clear ownership, policies, processes, metrics, governance, and measurable outcomes.
- Experience managing an enterprise portfolio of AI or technology tools, vendors

Life360’s mission is to keep people close to the ones they love. Our category-leading mobile app, Tile tracking devices, and Pet GPS tracker empower members to protect the people, pets, and things they care about most with a range of services, including location sharing, safe driver reports, and crash detection with emergency dispatch. Life360 serves approximately 100 million monthly active users across more than 180 countries.

Life360 delivers peace of mind and enhances everyday family life with seamless coordination for all the moments that matter, big and small. The team + the role

Pendo's Data Platform is the backbone of everything we do. Our systems process more than 50 billion events per day, peaking at over 1 million events per second, and manage dozens of petabytes of data across several production environments. The platform powers real-time data ingestion, batch processing, and analytics at scale — and the instrumentation standards that keep our entire codebase observable. It's built primarily in Go, runs on Google Kubernetes Engine, and relies on Cloud Pub/Sub, Firestore, Google Cloud Storage, Redis, and memcache. We expect the stack to evolve, and you'll help decide how.

We're looking for a Director of Engineering to lead the teams that own this infrastructure. This is a leadership role with real technical depth — you'll set strategy, build and grow high-performing engineering teams, and partner closely with Site Reliability Engineering. You'll stay close enough to the code to review designs, debug production issues, and contribute when it matters. You'll also own the economics of running the platform at this scale and be a trusted voice with customers on performance, data integrity, and reliability. If you want a role where architectural decisions have immediate business consequence and the technical bar is genuinely high, this is it.

This role is based in Raleigh, NC and follows Pendo's hybrid model: in-office 3 days per week.

What this looks like day-to-day
- Lead multiple engineering teams responsible for our real-time data ingestion pipeline, analytics batch job pipelines, and analytics query engine — setting technical direction and roadmap while balancing near-term delivery with long-term scalability, reliability, and cost efficiency.
- Drive architectural decisions across storage, compute, and data modeling; know when to adopt, build, or retire technologies and make those calls with conviction and clear rationale.
- Own instrumentation standards across the core codebase — structured logging, OpenTelemetry metrics and tracing — ensuring teams across the organization can adopt them with minimal friction and that the resulting telemetry is useful, consistent, and cost-conscious.
- Own the cost profile of the data platform at petabyte scale: forecast infrastructure spend for new product initiatives, improve cost attribution by customer, product, feature, and team, and diagnose and resolve cost overruns quickly.
- Partner with SRE on shared on-call responsibilities, incident response, postmortems, and reliability roadmaps; define and track SLOs for ingestion latency, query performance, and data correctness.
- Serve as a technical authority in customer conversations on platform performance, data integrity, and reliability — translating customer needs and escalations into clear engineering priorities.
- Hire, coach, and develop engineering managers and senior engineers; build a team culture grounded in high standards, clear communication, and continuous improvement.

PsiQuantum's mission is to build the first useful quantum computers: machines capable of delivering the breakthroughs the field has long promised. Since our founding in 2016, our singular focus has been to build and deploy million-qubit, fault-tolerant quantum systems.

Quantum computers harness the laws of quantum mechanics to solve problems that even the most advanced supercomputers or AI systems will never reach. Their impact will span energy, pharmaceuticals, finance, agriculture, transportation, materials, and other foundational industries.

Our architecture and approach is based on silicon photonics. By leveraging the advanced semiconductor manufacturing industry, including partners like GlobalFoundries, we use the same high-volume processes that already produce billions of chips for telecom and consumer electronics. Photonics offers natural advantages for scale: photons don't feel heat, are immune to electromagnetic interference, and integrate with existing cryogenic cooling and standard fiber-optic infrastructure.

That approach has since been tested at the highest level of scrutiny the U.S. government applies to emerging technology, and it has held up. In 2025, PsiQuantum closed a $1 billion funding round that valued the company at $7 billion. In 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce signed a $100 million Letter of Intent under the CHIPS and Science Act, followed by a $125 million agreement with DARPA under Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative, PsiQuantum's most valuable U.S. government agreement to date. This year, we also broke ground on our utility-scale quantum computer in Brisbane, Australia, and continued building out our Chicago site. SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. At the core of SambaNova's technology is the RDU (Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit) — a chip built on a dataflow architecture rather than the traditional GPU model. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

About the team

The IT team supports SambaNova’s employees and infrastructure. We manage the servers, networks, and cloud accounts our engineering teams use to build and test AI chips and systems. We also handle employee laptops, accounts, and software, and we run security across the company. The team is small and works closely with engineering and DevOps.

About the role

As Director of IT on the IT team, you will lead infrastructure, end-user IT, security operations, and DevOps support across the company. You will set the direction for the function and grow the team, and you will also do hands-on work when the team needs it. This role can be leveled at Director or Senior Director depending on experience.

Responsibilities
- Lead server and backend infrastructure, including on-prem and cloud systems, networking, storage, and identity
- Run desktop and end-user IT, including laptop provisioning, SaaS tools, help desk, and onboarding and off boarding
- Build and run the security program and security operations, including endpoint protection, access control, monitoring, and incident response
- Partner with engineering on DevOps tooling, CI/CD infrastructure, and automation
- Hire and manage the IT team, and set its roadmap and budget
- Manage vendors and contracts for IT and security tools
- Configure systems, troubleshoot outages, and write automation yourself when needed

Required qualifications
- B.S. in Computer Science, Information Technology, or related field
- 10+ years of experience in IT infrastructure and operations
- 5+ years of experience leading IT teams
- Experience running both backend infrastructure and end-user IT
- Experience building or running a security operations program
- Experience with DevOps tools such as Terraform, Ansible, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines
- Hands-on experience with Linux, Windows, and macOS administration, identity management such as Okta or Entra ID, and MDM
- Able to work onsite at our Bay Area office on a regular basis

Preferred qualifications
- Experience at a startup or high-growth company
- Experience supporting hardware or semiconductor engineering teams, including HPC or lab environments
- Experience with SOC 2, ISO 27001, or similar compliance programs
- Experience scaling an IT team through rapid headcount growth

About Treasury Prime

Treasury Prime is the operating layer for modern banking. We run the largest bank network for embedded finance, connecting 20+ banks with the fintechs they power through modern APIs. We’re a small, senior, fully remote team (Clojure, React, Postgres, AWS, and a growing set of AI agents) with a culture built on mutual respect, collaboration, and ownership. We’re backed by Y Combinator, QED Investors, Nyca Partners, Deciens Capital, SaaStr Fund, Susa Ventures, and others.

The Role

We're hiring a Vice President of Engineering to lead software engineering, DevOps, and data, and to serve on our executive team reporting to the CEO. You'll own how we build, ship, and run the platform banks and fintechs depend on every day.

This is a leadership role first. You're technical and can go deep on architecture and tradeoffs with your team, but your job is building a strong team, setting clear direction, and keeping engineering closely tied to customers and the rest of the business. You lead through influence, earn trust across functions, and bring people along when priorities or practices need to change.

At WelbeHealth, we serve our communities’ most vulnerable seniors through shared intention, pioneering spirit, and the courage to love. These core values and our participant focus lead the way no matter what.

The Director, IT Portfolio & Delivery provides leadership for enterprise technology portfolio planning, governance, delivery management, and performance visibility. Working closely with Technology leadership and business partners, this role translates strategy into an integrated portfolio of initiatives, establishes consistent delivery practices, and enables informed prioritization, sequencing, capacity, funding, and risk decisions.

This role is different because the Director, IT Portfolio & Delivery at WelbeHealth:
- Leads enterprise technology portfolio strategy, governance, and delivery, translating organizational priorities into an integrated roadmap of initiatives that drives business outcomes, optimizes resources, and supports WelbeHealth’s continued growth
- Builds and strengthens scalable delivery practices through data-driven decision-making, financial oversight, and cross-functional collaboration, ensuring technology investments are effectively prioritized, risks are proactively managed, and teams are equipped to deliver results

We care about our team members. That’s why we offer:
- Medical insurance coverage (Medical, Dental, Vision)
- Work/life balance - We mean it! 17 days of personal time off (PTO), 12 holidays observed annually, and 6 sick days
- 401K savings + match
- Comprehensive compensation package including base pay and bonus
- And additional benefits!

On the day-to-day, you will:
- Lead the enterprise Technology portfolio intake, assessment, prioritization, sequencing, and governance process, as well as translate Technology strategy and roadmaps into an integrated, executable portfolio with clear outcomes, milestones, dependencies, resource needs, and decision points
- Lead, coach, and develop Principal Scrum Masters and ITS Project Managers, including hiring, onboarding, goal setting, workload management, performance support, and succession planning, as well as assign delivery leadership based on initiative complexity, risk, methodology, and organizational priority
- Partner with Finance and Accounting teams to coordinate Technology capital expenditure planning, budgeting, forecasting, reporting, and reconciliation
- Maintain a reliable portfolio view of approved capital investments, forecasted spend, actual spend, commitments, variances, and expected completion timing
- Lead a Technology delivery center-of-excellence approach that defines, improves, and scales practical standards, templates, tools, and ways of working
- Assess current processes, identify root causes of friction or inconsistency, and lead cross-functional improvements that simplify work and strengthen accountability
- Build trusted relationships with executives, functional leaders, delivery teams, vendors, and other stakeholders, as well as manage

Trusted by industry leaders including Shopify, Paramount+, GM, Kroger, Fiserv, and NPCI, YugabyteDB has been deployed in over 100 countries and powers more than 5 million clusters worldwide.

Together, our hard-working team of experts and our industry-leading technology are uniquely positioned to meet the demands of modern workloads: geo-distributed, ultra-resilient, and built to scale without limits.

Our Yugabeings (distributed, like our database) span 12+ countries and multiple time zones, sharing expertise from diverse backgrounds and industries.

Yugabyte is the company behind YugabyteDB, the AI-ready, multi-modal, distributed PostgreSQL database for cloud-native apps. Trusted by industry leaders including Shopify, Paramount+, GM, Kroger, Fiserv, and NPCI, YugabyteDB has been deployed in over 100 countries and powers more than 5 million clusters worldwide.

Together, our hard-working team of experts and our industry-leading technology are uniquely positioned to meet the demands of modern workloads: geo-distributed, ultra-resilient, and built to scale without limits.

At Yugabyte, we are on a mission to build an open source, high-performance, distributed, and fault-tolerant PostgreSQL-compatible database for powering global, internet-scale applications. Our Database-as-a-Service (DBaaS) organization brings YugabyteDB to customers wherever they run: as a fully managed service on the major clouds with YugabyteDB Aeon, inside their own cloud accounts with Aeon BYOC, in their own data centers and Kubernetes environments with YugabyteDB Anywhere, and on a developer's laptop with yugabyted.

As the VP of Engineering for DBaaS, you will lead the teams that build, ship, and run every way customers consume YugabyteDB as a service. You will own the roadmap delivery, quality, and operation of YugabyteDB Aeon, Aeon BYOC, YugabyteDB Anywhere, and yugabyted. You will work across a modern cloud stack: Kubernetes on GKE, EKS, and AKS, Java frameworks, Python and shell automation, Terraform, and observability tooling across AWS, GCP, and Azure. You will be the executive owner of production for Aeon, setting the standard for incident response, on-call health, and the reliability our customers count on.

You will also own the Security and SRE charters for the DBaaS organization. That includes product and cloud security, vulnerability management, compliance programs such as SOC 2, and the SRE practices that keep Aeon highly available, performant, and cost-efficient around the clock. You will take responsibility for the resiliency, security, and cost of the architectural choices made across the organization, and stay close enough to the technology to lead design reviews and major incidents with your engineers.

You will lead a global organization of engineers, managers, and SREs across several geographies reporting to the SVP of Engineerin

Department: Information Technology

Description

The Vice President, Platform Engineering is a member of the Technology leadership team and is accountable for the technology platforms that power Align's digital products and operations: Data, AI, Cloud, API, and Identity. This leader sets the strategy, architecture, and operating model for these platforms and treats them as products that let engineering and business teams build faster, more securely, and at scale.

The VP translates business needs into a coherent platform architecture and serves as the primary technical and business authority on Align's platform capabilities. Responsibilities span engineering, securing, and optimizing cloud infrastructure; building a trusted, well-governed data foundation; delivering shared AI and machine learning capabilities with responsible AI guardrails; and providing secure identity and API services for workforce, customer, and partner ecosystems. The role ensures all platforms meet regulatory and compliance requirements, including SOX, PCI DSS, and applicable privacy regulations.

This leader builds and scales high-performing engineering teams and partners closely with R&D, product, security, and business stakeholders. Strong technical depth, influential leadership, and the ability to drive change in a complex, fast-moving enterprise environment are essential.

The role reports to the Chief Digital Officer and is located in San Jose, CA, or Raleigh, NC.

• Operate the platforms as products, with clear internal customers, service levels, adoption metrics, and feedback loops, so product and engineering teams can build faster and more reliably.

• Partner with the Chief Digital Officer, business unit leaders, R&D, product, security, and infrastructure teams to translate business needs into platform capabilities and build consensus on architecture and investment priorities.

• Own platform budgets, vendor strategy, and build-versus-buy decisions. Lead technology evaluations, RFI/RFP processes, proofs of concept, and vendor negotiations.

• Establish architecture standards, reference patterns, and governance that drive modular, reusable, and well-abstracted solutions across the product and enterprise portfolio.

Data Platform

You'll work alongside software architects, hardware engineers, systems engineers, AI researchers, product leaders, program managers, and operational experts to turn complex mission requirements into scalable, reusable technology solutions.

You'll establish the engineering standards, architecture principles, technical review processes, and development practices that allow Astrion to move faster without compromising quality, security, reliability, or mission performance.

Pickett, an ESP Associates company, is a highly innovative surveying and engineering company with over 60 years of industry experience serving clients throughout the US and Caribbean.

“We solve the problems that matter” and we are always looking to add passionate, motivated, and qualified individuals to our rapidly expanding team.

As the Vice President of Engineering, you will play a critical leadership role in our organization.

This role will be responsible for not only managing the technical engineering team(s) but also the department’s operational, financial, and strategic functions. • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Electrical or Civil preferred); Master’s degree or MBA preferred

At Foundant, we build mission-critical software for the social good ecosystem — helping foundations, grantmakers, nonprofits, and community organizations streamline their work, strengthen relationships, and maximize their impact. We serve the giving community worldwide with a comprehensive suite of solutions spanning grant management, community foundation software, and giving analytics.

We're a unified company shaped by strong roots across our product portfolio, and we operate with intention and purpose. Our team of ~350 people across six countries is connected by a shared North Star: to be the trusted partner and strategic advisor to the communities we serve.

Our culture is collaborative, open, and inclusive. We believe in continuous improvement, accessible design, and a supportive environment that encourages experimentation and growth.

• With office locations in Bozeman, MT, Toronto, Canada, and Dublin, Ireland, you'll be part of a globally connected team. Job Description Summary

The Director, Infrastructure & Platform leads the team that creates standard, reliable environments on which Defense & Systems builds, tests, and delivers software. The team owns the secure platforms, shared services, and the single golden-path delivery pipeline that the organization's software developers depend on, so that delivery is dependable, on time, and to standard. The role runs the platform as a product, not as a help desk.

This is a people-leadership role accountable for both the operating model and the people who run it. The Director sets the platform roadmap and service standards, mandates the golden path that product teams adopt, and holds the team to FLIGHT DECK standard work and a bias toward flow. Success improves Safety, Quality, Delivery, and Cost by removing undifferentiated infrastructure work from every software team and replacing ad-hoc environments with a governed, consumable platform.

Job Description

Roles and Responsibilities

Team leadership and talent

• Lead and develop the Infrastructure & Platform team — technical program management, platform and infrastructure engineering, and infrastructure architecture — with clear role clarity, objectives, and standard work for each seat
• Own the team’s performance and development; build a culture of ownership, flow, and continuous improvement
• Identify and remove obstacles on behalf of the team, and coach problem-solving at the point of work

Platform operating model and governance

• Own and mandate a single golden-path delivery pipeline — CI/CD, environments, and shared services — that all product teams adopt, and govern the exception process when a team cannot
• Operate the platform as a product: a named backlog, a published roadmap, and service standards for availability, support, change management, and SLAs
• Establish how platform change is requested, prioritized, approved, and released, and make that governance visible to the teams it affects
• Partner with Cyber Security to build security best practice into the platform by default, and scope the DevSecOps capability gap as an explicit Phase 2 headcount ask

Delivery and reliability

• Ensure secure, reliable, and scalable infrastructure across cloud, on-premises, and edge environments in a defense context
• Set the operating rhythm — daily management, WOR, and MOR — that keeps reliability and delivery managed, not merely reported
• Partner with the four product-development software teams so the platform meets their current needs and anticipates their future ones

Cross-organization alignment

• Represent Infrastructure & Platform in the Tech Ops leadership cadence and align the platform roadmap to the enterprise and CDAIO baseline
• Partner with the Director, Architecture & Data so platform patterns and architecture guardrails stay coupled

Basic Qualifications (required)

• Bachelor's degree from an accredited university or college with a minimum of 7 years of professional experience OR Ass

Location: Remote United States

Compensation: Up to $400,000 base salary

Ready to apply Before you do, make sure to read all the details pertaining to this job in the description below.

About the Company

Our client is an award-winning, healthcare technology company transforming how chronic and remote care is delivered across the United States. Trusted by 2,000+ providers and supporting 150,000+ patients nationwide, they deliver AI-enabled care management solutions, including Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM) and Chronic Care Management (CCM), that measurably improve outcomes, reduce costs, and close care gaps.

The company is HIPAA and SOC 2 Type II compliant, integrates with 50+ EMR systems.

The Role

This is not a traditional CTO hire. We're looking for a hands-on AI agent builder, someone who writes code daily, ships production AI systems, and can architect the next generation of autonomous clinical care agents, while carrying the CTO title and owning the full technology vision.

The company sits on a goldmine of real-time patient data (vitals, device telemetry, EMR records, clinical notes) flowing from 150,000+ monitored patients. The opportunity is to build intelligent agents that act on that data: triaging alerts, predicting deterioration, automating care coordination workflows, and augmenting clinical decision-making at scale. You'll be building this largely from scratch with a small, high-caliber team.

What You'll Build
• Autonomous Clinical Agents: Design and ship AI agents that monitor patient data streams in real time, escalate intelligently, and automate care coordination tasks that today require manual clinical effort.
• LLM-Powered Workflows: Build agent pipelines using large language models for clinical note summarization, patient communication, care plan generation, and intelligent triage.
• Predictive & Preventive Models: Develop and deploy models for risk stratification, readmission prediction, and early deterioration detection across chronic disease populations.
• Agent Orchestration: Architect multi-agent systems that coordinate across data ingestion, clinical reasoning, provider notification, and patient engagement, with appropriate human-in-the-loop safeguards for healthcare.
• Data Infrastructure: Build the real-time data pipelines and feature stores that feed your agents, patient vitals from connected devices, EMR data via HL7/FHIR, and unstructured clinical documentation.
• EMR Integration Layer: Extend and harden integrations across 50+ EMR/EHR systems to ensure agents can read from and write back to provider workflows seamlessly.

Who You Are
• You ship AI systems, not slide decks. You're writing Python/TypeScript daily, prototyping agent architectures, and pushing to production. You've built and deployed LLM-based agents, RAG pipelines, or autonomous workflows in a production environment.

About Leadex Systems

Leadex Systems builds integration and API management platforms for banks, payment providers and government entities across the Middle East, Cyprus and Europe. We are 60 people. We have been a Mule Soft partner for years and were named Mule Soft Partner of the Year Middle East 2024 and Mule Soft Partner Champion Middle East 2025. Most of what we build lives in places where an integration failure is a regulatory event rather than a bad sprint: core banking, payments, onboarding, government service platforms.

Our clients run central bank audits, ISO 20022 migrations and multi-year complex implementations. We sit in the middle of complex digital transformations as an integration team connecting overall IT/IS landscape together.
What this role is

We are hiring a CTO to own the technical side of the company: how we design solutions, how we deliver them, and how our engineering organisation grows. You will report directly to founder (and current CTO) and CEO and sit on the leadership team. Day to day the job splits roughly three ways: architecture on our most complex programs, technical leadership of a distributed delivery team, and the engineering half of presales, where you shape the solution and defend it in front of a client's architecture board.

Our delivery portfolio today is mostly Mule Soft and Salesforce. We are not looking for a Mule Soft specialist. We are looking for an engineer who has spent a career on integration, has run genuinely hard programs, and can learn a platform in a quarter. If you have never touched Anypoint, we will get you through certification. What we cannot teach is the judgment that comes from having personally untangled a 200-interface landscape under a regulator's deadline.

• Engineering standards across the practice. Integration patterns, API design, CI/CD and release strategy, non-functional requirements, how we estimate. Today these live in people's heads and in past project artefacts; we want them written down and enforced.

Founded on the principle of democratizing access, first to music in 1999, now to expertise in the AI era, Napster has consistently remained at the forefront of technological shifts that empower users. Today, the company builds embodied, multimodal AI agents that engage employees and customers where they already work: through video presence, voice, and text. Designed to work alongside people rather than replace them, Napster's agents carry institutional knowledge into every interaction, elevating the user's experience and improving business outcomes. For more information, visit napster.com.

We are looking for a senior Vice President of Technology Partnerships & Partner Engineering to lead the organization responsible for the technical success, activation, and scale of our strategic technology partner ecosystem.

This is an executive-level role combining technical depth, commercial judgment, organizational leadership, and operational discipline. The VP will work across Partnerships, Channel, Sales, Product, and Engineering to turn strategic relationships into technically validated, activated, and commercially productive partnerships.

The role sits at the intersection of partner strategy, partner engineering, pre-sales, product, and commercial execution. It is not a quota-carrying sales role and is not an engineering delivery function. Its mandate is to ensure strategic partners have the technical engagement, resources, solutions, integrations, and internal alignment needed to move from opportunity through validation, activation, and scale.

• Build and lead the Technology Partnerships & Partner Engineering organization, including team structure, coverage model, operating rhythm, and talent development.

The company designs, develops, and operates hospitality-driven destinations to host gatherings of all kinds, ranging from small corporate meetings to immersive brand activations and beyond. We love bringing people together in person, and that passion for great experiences extends to our employees as well.

If you're interested in creating inspiring moments of connection, consider joining our team.
Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. You’ll lead through the platform, redesigning how we deploy and setting the standards our product and corporate engineering teams build on. You'll also run the cloud, AI, and venue infrastructure under our portfolio of brands, from client-facing experiences to the systems that keep our nearly 40 venues running.

This is a rebuild. You design it and you build it.

Today, deployments are manual and happen about once a sprint. That's the starting line. You'll rethink how we ship so that deployments are unlocked, safe, secure, and governed.

You'll have high autonomy and real decision-making power over the tools we use and how we build. We're committed to AWS and will build deeply on it. Most of what sits on top is fair game: CI tooling, pipeline design, orchestration patterns, and source control. A decision like Bitbucket versus Git Hub is a live call, and it's yours to make.

Legacy migration follows the decisions. You make the call, then you do the move. This role will have a lot of influence.

This is a wide seat. You’ll work across product and corporate engineering, and you’re a big part of how we get to AI-first, spec-driven development.

• Rebuild the deployment path. Own CI/CD end to end: build, release, and rollback. Take us from manual deploys to an automated path.

• Make the platform calls. Source control, CI tooling, orchestration, and infrastructure-as-code patterns. Jenkins is what we run today; what we run next is up to you. Decide, document the trade-off, then go forth and migrate.

Patrick Industries, a publicly traded company headquartered in Elkhart, Indiana, invites you to join a team of dedicated Team Members who are passionate about delivering high-quality products and exceptional customer service. As a leading solutions provider serving a diverse range of markets across the United States, our commitment to innovation, quality, and sustainability has positioned us as a high growth, diversified and empowered Team of more than 10,000! Your adventure awaits!

Patrick Industries is building its enterprise AI and data capability from the ground up — and is searching for the executive to lead it. The leader drives clear traceability from each use case to defined KPIs and business outcomes, strengthens the data-governance leg of the enterprise Digital Backbone, and aligns delivery to Patrick’s IT Strategic Pillars:
• Innovative Advantage – Scale AI-, data-, and automation-driven capabilities that unlock new business value.
• Value Optimization – Ensure measurable ROI, efficiency gains, and capital discipline.

Lead the initiative's governance and operating cadence, including an executive steering committee, portfolio prioritization, funding decisions, and regular progress, risk, and ROI reporting out to the executive leadership team, CEO and Board as appropriate. ABOUT Resources Legacy Fund (RLF):

Resources Legacy Fund builds the architecture behind lasting environmental progress. From climate resilience to land and water conservation to community well-being, we help visionary ideas take shape—offering the steady support and strategic know-how to turn complex challenges into collective victories.

We deliver transformative outcomes for our planet and its people through trusted partnerships and creative campaigns. Rooted in California and expanding across Western North America and beyond, we have a 25-year track record of supporting initiatives at every scale. We also host fiscally sponsored projects that reach across the globe, reinforcing the efforts of change makers worldwide.

Addressing three interconnected crises — climate change, biodiversity loss, and environmental injustice — requires creativity, collaboration, and fast reflexes. With deep operational expertise and the confidence of donors and partners, we enable lasting solutions to rise.

About Charm
 
Our mission is to return the atmosphere to 280 ppm CO₂. We convert excess inedible biomass into carbon-rich bio-oil and inject it into underground storage for permanent carbon removal. At scale, we can use bio-oil to make fossil-free iron.
 
Our carbon removal efforts began in 2020 with initial purchases from customers like Stripe, Shopify, and Microsoft. Since then, we’ve scaled to thousands of tons of carbon removal, grown to over a hundred employees, and established three locations in San Francisco, Colorado, and Louisiana.
 
We're expanding our team of ambitious, creative, and hands-on problem solvers. We value psychological safety, collaboration, and continuous learning. We take calculated risks and treat mistakes as opportunities to improve. If you're excited about tackling big challenges, we encourage you to explore our company values.
 
Come help us reverse climate change. Gigatons or bust!


About the Role
The Director of Program and Systems Engineering owns how Charm plans, builds, and delivers new systems across Biomass, Pyrolysis, and Injection workstreams by cultivating a deep understanding of Charm’s business strategy and technology roadmaps. You and your team will run the program portfolio and own the system-level architecture, requirements maintenance, and workcenter interfaces that tie feedstock processing, pyrolysis production, bio-oil and biochar inventory handling, and injection operations together. 
You will build and lead a team of technical program managers and engineering staff members who fabricate, assemble, and commission new pyrolysis and injection systems, bringing designs from concept to real world, steady-state operation. About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor is hiring a Head of Hardware Engineering to lead the team that designs and builds our robots. Mechanical, electrical, firmware and embedded, and manufacturing engineering all report to this role. You set the hardware roadmap with the CTO, you grow the team, and you are responsible for every robot we ship working as designed and building at the rate we need. You report to the CTO.
The hardware organization will grow a lot, in people and in the range of products it covers. The person in this role builds the teams that make that happen, hires the people who lead them, and keeps the whole thing running well as it gets bigger.

Requirements
- You have led and grown a hardware engineering organization to 50 or more people, and shipped a complex electromechanical product in volume through it
- You have led mechanical, electrical, and firmware or embedded engineers, and can hire and judge all three
- You have owned manufacturing engineering, or worked closely enough with it to build that team: process, test, fixtures, and design for manufacturing
- You have developed the managers who lead teams under you
- You have worked closely with a technical founder or CTO
Nice to haves
- Robotics, actuators, or motion control
- Leading engineers in more than one country
- Taking a product from first prototype to producti

Picture yourself brightening someone’s day. When you join our Hotels team, that’s exactly what you’ll do every time you come to work! As a  Property Operations Director , you’re not just responsible for the safety and functionality of the property – you’re spreading the light and warmth of hospitality by delivering memorable experiences that make the stay for every guest.

Here's what you'll do during a typical day:
- Lead facility operations: Direct the functionality, safety, and compliance of the hotel’s buildings, mechanical systems, electrical systems, HVAC, life safety systems, and grounds in accordance with federal, state, and local regulations
- Oversee facility maintenance: Conduct facility inspections, maintain documentation for energy management and conservation programs, and oversee preventive maintenance initiatives
- Direct property improvements: Lead capital projects and property rehabilitations – including scheduling, budgeting, contractor bidding, and licensing/permitting – while ensuring regulatory compliance

- Cultivate a high-performing team: Drive engagement and retention through performance management, professional development, and recognition programs

At Hilton, our core values define what it takes to succeed here and guide the qualities we look for in every team member:
A passion for spreading the light and warmth of Hospitality . Acting with Integrity and always doing the right thing. Inspiring others through Leadership . A belief that Teamwork drives the best outcomes. A sense of Ownership and accountability. And a focus on the Now , bringing urgency and discipline to every moment, knowing it can make a lasting impact.

Join an Award-Winning Workplace Culture

At Hilton, we don’t just deliver exceptional experiences for our guests—we build an exceptional workplace for the Team Members who make it all possible. As a global leader in hospitality, we’ve welcomed more than 3 billion guests worldwide, all while staying true to our founding vision: to fill the earth with the light and warmth of hospitality.

Our award-winning culture has earned us repeated recognition on the World’s Best Workplaces list by Great Place to Work and Fortune. With our suite of world-class brands ,  and a company-wide commitment to providing the best stay for every guest, we’re setting new standards for the future of travel.

Whether you’re starting your career or exploring something new, Hilton supports your journey every step of the way. Come for the job, stay for the career—and help us make every stay a little more magical.

Curious about life at Hilton? Explore our  Careers Blog  to see why we’re more than a great place to stay—we’re a great place to work.

At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

This position plays a critical part in enabling scalable, repeatable performance by coaching leaders, orchestrating strategic improvement processes, and ensuring the AOS framework becomes deeply institutionalized throughout the enterprise.

- Coordinate, prioritize, and organize Improvement Events.

As a Senior Director of eSoftware Engineering in JPMorgan Chase’s Commercial and Investment Bank, you will join the Equities Electronic Trading Technology team as a core, hands-on engineer on our ultra-low-latency trading platform. You will design, build, and optimize the latency-critical C++ that powers our electronic trading business, spanning the core platform, high-performance market data, order execution, and market-making systems that price and quote equities and equity derivatives.
This senior-leadership-backed investment in our people and platform will help define the next generation of electronic trading. Our engineers work across ultra-low-latency trading technology, systematic trading, next-generation high-performance market data, and the core platform that brings them together. Disciplined prioritization and research-driven product development guide this work.
If you have deep expertise in low-latency C++ and want to write code whose performance is measured in nanoseconds—with a direct impact on clients and the business—this is the team for you.
Job responsibilities
- Designs, builds, and optimizes latency-critical components of the core trading platform in modern C++, including the threading and event-processing model, inter-component messaging, memory management, and networking layers that market data, market-making, and execution applications are built on
- Partners with traders and quantitative researchers to build and evolve electronic market-making systems, including quoting and quote management, real-time pricing and hedging, and pre-trade risk controls that meet regulatory and firm control requirements
- Treats latency as a measured quantity: builds instrumentation, benchmarks, and profiling into the platform, and drives down tail latency and jitter through data-driven optimization
- Works across the software/hardware boundary, including CPU caches, NUMA, core isolation, kernel-bypass networking, and hardware timestamping, partnering with infrastructure and network engineering on host and colocation tuning
- Develops secure, high-quality, well-tested production code, reviews and debugs code written by others, and helps set the platform’s engineering standards for performance, correctness, and design
- Owns systems in production, diagnosing issues quickly during live trading and automating remediation of recurring issues to improve operational stability
- Adds to team culture of diversity, opportunity, inclusion, and respect

Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
- Formal training or certification on software engineering concepts and 10+ years applied experience. In addition, 5+ years of experience leading technologists to manage, anticipate and solve complex technical items within your domain of expertise and more broadly across the organization
- Expert-level

Job Overview
We are seeking a highly experienced and hands-on technology leader to drive the strategy, architecture, development, and modernization of customer-facing and internal digital platforms. This role requires deep expertise in full-stack engineering, cloud-native architectures, AI-enabled solutions, and large-scale enterprise application development.
The successful candidate will play a critical role in shaping customer acquisition, onboarding, servicing, AML verification, customer journey orchestration, and self-service experiences across digital channels. This individual will provide technical leadership, influence engineering teams, contribute directly to architecture and solution design, and drive the adoption of emerging technologies including Generative AI and Agentic AI.
This is primarily a technology leadership role requiring strong hands-on engineering and architecture capabilities, while also providing mentorship and technical guidance to engineering teams.

What You'll Do
- Lead design and development of enterprise-scale digital applications.
- Architect and build APIs, microservices, and cloud-native solutions.
- Drive adoption of AI, Generative AI, LLMs, and AI-assisted engineering tools.
- Partner with business and product teams to deliver customer-focused solutions.
- Mentor engineers and champion engineering excellence, quality, and innovation.
- Modernize legacy platforms and build reusable frameworks and services.

- 15+ years of software engineering and technology leadership experience.
- Strong hands-on expertise in: Java, Spring Boot, Python React, Angular, JavaScript Microservices and API Development MongoDB, DB2, Oracle, RDBMS/NoSQL Cloud Platforms, Containers, CI/CD
- Experience building customer-facing digital products and platforms.
- Knowledge of Generative AI, AI Agents, RAG, LLMs, and AI-powered development tools.
- Strong understanding of software architecture, design patterns, and scalable solution design.
Preferred Experience
- Digital Banking or Financial Services
- Customer Acquisition & Onboarding Platforms
- Customer Experience & Self-Service Channels
- AML / Compliance Solutions
- Contact Center & IVR Integrations
Why Join Us?
Join a high-performing engineering organization where you'll influence technology strategy, drive AI-led innovation, and build next-generation digital experiences that impact millions of customers.

About the Role
Join Controls Technology division as a Technology Product Owner. In this critical role, you will act as the bridge between complex business needs and our engineering teams. You will be empowered to translate intricate requirements for risk and control systems into a flawlessly managed backlog of epics and user stories. Your primary mission is to drive the delivery of high-quality, compliant software by ensuring our development teams have the clarity and context needed to execute effectively, sprint after sprint. This is a role for a product owner — someone who thrives on execution, champions quality, and is passionate about building world-class technology solutions in a dynamic, global financial environment.

What You'll Do
1. Backlog Ownership & Agile Execution
- Own and Master the Backlog: Meticulously create, refine, and prioritize the product backlog, ensuring it is transparent, well-understood, and always ready for at least two sprints ahead.
- Translate Vision into Action: Deconstruct complex business requirements into well-defined Epics, User Stories, and precise Acceptance Criteria, ensuring a high percentage of stories are accepted without rework.
- Drive Sprint Success: Serve as the dedicated point of contact for the engineering team, providing unwavering clarity during sprint planning, daily stand-ups, and throughout the development cycle to remove ambiguity.
2. Solution Definition & Quality Assurance
- Define the "What": Partner with business stakeholders to elicit, analyze, and document requirements, defining the precise solution to be built.
- Champion Quality: Drive a quality-first mindset with a relentless focus on clear, testable acceptance criteria to minimize ambiguity and reduce critical defects in UAT.
- Demonstrate Value: Conduct compelling demos of new functionalities to stakeholders, showcasing the value delivered and gathering immediate feedback for iterative improvement.
3. Stakeholder Collaboration & Domain Leadership
- Build Partnerships: Act as the key liaison between business users, engineering teams, UX and other technology partners, fostering a collaborative environment to ensure seamless delivery.
- Become the SME: Develop a deep expertise in your assigned Controls Technology modules, becoming the recognized go-to subject matter expert for the team and key stakeholders.
- Facilitate with Purpose: Lead and actively contribute to all agile ceremonies, ensuring refinement and planning sessions are efficient, productive, and outcome focused.
4. Innovation in Execution
- Leverage AI Tools: Utilize cutting-edge AI tools to accelerate requirements analysis, improve the quality of user story documentation, and enhance feature file generation.
- Mitigate Risk Proactively: Identify and flag potential risks and dependencies that could impact schedule or quality, and work with leadership to drive mitigation strategies.

We are looking for an experienced AI Engineer to design, develop, and deploy enterprise-grade AI solutions that transform how Third-Party Management teams assess, monitor, and manage supplier and vendor risks.
This role combines software engineering, AI engineering, analytics, and product development to build intelligent applications that improve operational efficiency, decision quality, and user experience. The successful candidate will partner closely with business stakeholders, data engineers, technology teams, and AI governance partners to deliver scalable AI capabilities aligned with enterprise standards.

Key Responsibilities
AI Solution Development

- Develop AI-powered copilots, knowledge assistants, workflow automation, and decision-support tools.
- Build reusable AI services, APIs, and components for enterprise adoption.
- Develop multi-agent workflows for complex business processes.
Knowledge Engineering

- Build document ingestion, metadata extraction, semantic search, and retrieval pipelines.

- Ensure knowledge assets remain governed, traceable, and reusable.
Software Engineering
- Build scalable Python-based backend services and APIs.
- Develop modern web applications using enterprise UI frameworks.
- Integrate AI services with internal data platforms and enterprise applications.
- Write clean, modular, and production-ready code.
AI Governance
- Ensure AI solutions comply with enterprise governance, security, and model risk requirements.
- Support model evaluation, monitoring, auditability, and explainability.
- Collaborate with AI governance teams on documentation and deployment approvals.
Collaboration
- Partner with business stakeholders to understand challenges and identify AI opportunities.
- Work closely with technology, architecture, cybersecurity, and data engineering teams.
- Support production deployment and operationalization of AI solutions.
- Mentor junior engineers and contribute to AI engineering best practices.

Required Qualifications
- Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Engineering, Mathematics, or related discipline. Master’s degree preferred.
- Significant experience in software engineering, AI engineering, analytics, or data science.
- Strong Python programming skills.
- Experience building REST APIs and backend applications.
- Knowledge of SQL and data engineering concepts.
- Experience working with cloud platforms and enterprise application development.
- Strong problem-solving and stakeholder management skills.
- Excellent written and verbal communication.

Preferred Qualifications
Experience in one or more of the following:
- LLM application development

The Services Technology Modernization/Transformation program is a strategic, multi-year initiative to modernize our core platforms by migrating to an OpenShift environment on Prem and later onto Public Cloud. This transformation is fundamentally redesigning our operating model, impacting the roadmap of various business-critical applications and anchoring a deliberate journey from legacy monolithic systems to resilient, cloud-native microservices.
The Application Platform Cloud Solutions Engineer is a senior, independent leader responsible for engineering and defining the target state technical architecture for critical domains within this program. This role is technology-focused; it is centered on shaping the future of our function by defining technical capabilities, end-to-end processes, data flows, controls, and network connectivity across both private (on-prem OpenShift/Kubernetes) and public cloud (AWS/GCP) environments. You will be the primary driver in translating strategic goals into a coherent business/technology blueprint that will guide the transformation, including the decomposition of monolithic applications into microservices and the design of secure, resilient connectivity between on-prem applications, clients, market data providers, and payments networks.
Reporting to the Infra and Platform Lead, you will work with a small team of application architects and with senior stakeholders across Business, Operations, and Technology to ensure the program's success from a business process, engineering, and functional perspective.

Key Responsibilities

The Vice President (VP) / Senior Software Engineer – Technical Remediation & Enablement Lead is a hands-on, code-level technical specialist responsible for driving the direct remediation of software vulnerabilities across enterprise application teams. This individual contributor / team-level technical lead works alongside application developers and contractor engineers to fix static code vulnerabilities (SAST), patch vulnerable software dependencies (SCA/third-party libraries), containerize workloads, and streamline local build/release pipelines to achieve same-day vulnerability hotfix and deployment capabilities .
This role combines active software engineering (writing/refactoring code and debugging pipelines) with technical enablement, guiding squad developers on how to adopt internal security and build tools, resolve tricky dependency conflicts, and package applications into modern containers for rapid, low-risk production releases.

1. Hands-On Code Remediation & Dependency Patching
- Write, refactor, and review application code to directly remediate static code analysis (SAST) findings (e.g., SQL/command injection, cross-site scripting, insecure deserialization, improper error handling, weak cryptography).
- Resolve complex third-party library and framework upgrades (SCA/CVE remediation), managing transitive dependency conflicts, breaking API changes, and version incompatibilities across Java, Python, Go, .NET, or JavaScript/TypeScript stacks.
- Implement targeted automated unit, integration, and regression tests to validate that code fixes and patched libraries do not introduce functional regressions.

- Work directly in application repositories to write and optimize Dockerfile s, container manifests, and base image configurations (Docker, OCI, Kubernetes/OpenShift).

- Help configure and fine-tune CI/CD build scripts and release pipelines to compress deployment cycle times and eliminate manual deployment steps for emergency hotfixes.
3. Application Plan Technical Validation
- Perform code-level reviews of proposed remediation plans from application teams, verifying whether proposed library version bumps or refactored logic effectively eliminate the root cause of the vulnerability.
- Identify technical prerequisites (e.g., test coverage gaps, build tool upgrades, compiler/runtime updates) needed before a team can successfully patch and release.
4. Contractor Squad Pairing & PR Review
- Act as a peer reviewer and technical guide for external contractor engineers assigned to assist with remediation work.

Role Overview
The Enterprise Architecture Manager is a strategic senior technical leader responsible for defining, directing, and governing the enterprise target state architecture, technology portfolio lifecycle, and modernization roadmap across Citi's global technology estate.
In this role, you will lead the transformation of application architecture governance, software and infrastructure inventory management, data analytics capabilities, and the operationalization of next-generation enterprise AI patterns. Operating at the intersection of business strategy, enterprise architecture, and emerging AI technologies, you will partner with senior technology, risk, compliance, and business leaders to drive enterprise-wide modernization programs, elevate data quality, mitigate technical debt, and ensure continuous regulatory and audit readiness.
Key Responsibilities
1. Enterprise Architecture Governance & Strategic Modernization
- Target State Architecture (TSA) & Blueprints: Define, govern, and maintain the Enterprise Target State Architecture, Transition Roadmaps, and Reference Architectures across all domains: Business, Data, Application, Technology, and Security (BDATS) .
- Architecture Governance Framework: Operationalize Architecture Review Boards (ARBs), establish enterprise Architecture Decision Records (ADRs), and enforce adherence to standard frameworks (e.g., TOGAF 10, BIAN ).
- Application & Infrastructure Portfolio Management (APM): Oversee global application inventory, software asset lifecycles, and CMDB data fidelity to eliminate architectural debt, manage obsolescence, and support cloud migration and legacy modernization initiatives.
- Root Cause & Impact Analysis: Conduct in-depth technical investigations, Root Cause Analyses (RCA), and structural impact assessments on core operating platforms to engineer proactive systemic guardrails.
2. Multi-Agent Systems, Autonomous Engineering & AI Architecture
- Autonomous AI & Developer Platforms (Devin AI / AI Engineering): Architect and integrate autonomous software engineering agents and AI coding platforms (e.g., Devin AI , GitHub Copilot Workspace, Cursor, Claude Code) into the enterprise Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC), establishing secure sandboxing, verification pipelines, architectural compliance gates, and automated code review guardrails.
- Agentic Orchestration & Patterns: Architect enterprise-grade pattern-based multi-agent systems utilizing frameworks such as Salesforce Agentic Architecture, LangGraph/AutoGen, and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) orchestration patterns (Supervisor-Worker, Hierarchical Planning, ReAct).
- Model Context Protocol (MCP) Integration: Define and implement Model Context Protocol (MCP) standards and secure tool-calling interfaces to decouple LLMs and autonomous agents from backend enterprise services, databases, and microservices.
- Knowledge Graphs & Semantic Ontologies: Architect Enterprise Architecture Knowledge Graphs (EAKG) using open semantic ontologies

About San Francisco Public Library
The San Francisco Public Library (SFPL) connects our diverse communities to learning, opportunities, and each other. The library system includes the architecturally significant Main Library, an anchor institution in the city's Civic Center, 27 neighborhood branch libraries that serve all neighborhoods throughout the city, two administrative buildings and four bookmobiles. With a collection of more than 5 million items, and circulation exceeding 14.5 million each year, SFPL serves more than 4.5 million visitors annually.
The library embraces its role as the most democratic of institutions, providing safe and welcoming facilities for all. Through a robust array of services and programs, the library is dedicated to advancing literacy and learning, serving as a cultural amplifier, acting as a catalyst for community engagement, guiding patrons as a thoughtful navigator, and providing essential resources to support healthy, equitable communities. For more information about SFPL, please visit www.sfpl.org .
SFPL Statement on Racial Equity:
SFPL must build a culture, space and workplace that is accessible and welcoming to all current and future employees and to actively build an environment in which all people regardless of background, identity, or ability, can be equal participants. In this way, our staff at all organizational levels can reflect the communities we serve. A safe, equitable public library is an actively anti-racist public library. Creating an inclusive public library means aligning with the lived realities of people of color. SFPL is committed to advancing racial equity for our workforce and community, and will actively engage in anti-racist practice programs, and collection development in carrying out the Library's mission.

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.
Why join the Harvard Radcliffe Institute?
The Radcliffe Institute for Advanced Study at Harvard University, known colloquially as Harvard Radcliffe Institute, is one of the world’s leading centers for interdisciplinary exploration. We bring together students, scholars, artists, and practitioners to pursue curiosity-driven research, expand human understanding, and grapple with questions that demand insight from across disciplines.
The Fellowship Program annually supports the work of 50 leading artists and scholars. Academic Ventures fosters collaborative research projects and sponsors lectures and conferences that engage scholars with the public. The Schlesinger Library documents the lives of American women of the past and present for the future, furthering the Institute's commitment to women, gender, and society. The Emerging Leaders Program is a youth leadership development program partnering local high school sophomores with Harvard undergraduates in a mentoring relationship.
The Institute’s work is shaped by its history as the former Radcliffe College—a school founded to ensure that the standard of education embodied in Harvard was accessible to women, who were then excluded from the University. But the legacy of Radcliffe College is not simply coeducation at Harvard; it is the recognition that universities will always be greater when they draw wisdom and talent from the widest possible pool.
Take a look at this video to get different staff perspectives on working at Harvard Radcliffe Institute !
