This position will serve as the leader of workload and performance analysis, hardware/software (HW/SW) optimization and co-design (including AI workloads), and SoC architecture. Expertise in architecture, design, validation, HW/SW optimization, and co-design is required. Experience in platform design and translating customer-facing requirements into system-level requirements is highly desirable.
The role encompasses workload characterization, solution integration, performance and power tradeoffs, the development of advanced SoC architecture, modeling methodologies, and design enablement strategies across multiple product lines.
The ideal candidate is a recognized technical leader with deep expertise in workload and performance analysis, AI workloads, HW/SW co-design, and SoC architecture. You will partner with product groups, platform teams, and executive leadership to define and analyze products and SoCs for performance and workload analysis, and help co-optimize using next-generation design methodologies that accelerate innovation and enable reuse across the organization.
Key Responsibilities
Technical Leadership
- Define and drive the strategic roadmap for workload analysis and performance for both IPs and products across the company.
- Lead architecture performance reviews and technical direction for complex IP/SoC and subsystem developments.
- Establish best practices for hardware/software co-design and model-based development.
- Provide technical leadership for cross-functional teams spanning architecture, design, verification, emulation, and software.

AI-Driven Engineering Innovation
- Define and analyze AI workloads and the performance required for these workloads.

Organizational Leadership
- Build and lead high-performing engineering teams.
- Mentor directors, principal engineers, and distinguished engineers.
- Foster collaboration across Central Engineering, Product Groups, and external partners.
- Influence long-term semiconductor technology and platform strategy.

Education
- MS or Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical discipline (Ph.D. highly desired).

Experience
- 15+ years of experience in semiconductor or SoC development.
- 8+ years of technical leadership experience.
- Proven experience leading performance and workload analysis and HW/SW co-optimization.

Technical Skills
- Strong understanding of:
- Performance analysis
- Workload analysis
- AI workloads
- SoC architecture and integration
- Digital design methodologies
- IP and subsystem development
- Hardware/software co-design
- SoC verification methodologies
- Hands-on experience with:
- Performance and workload benchmarking
- Virtual platforms and executable specifications
- SoC performance modeling
- Design and verification automation flows

WHY SAP SUCCESSFACTORS
SAP SuccessFactors is the HCM system of record for some of the world's largest and most complex organizations. Our advantage is not just product breadth; it is the enterprise data foundation that underpins everything we build: workforce, financial, and operational data across every major industry, in 160 countries. No point solution can match it.
We are now at the most exciting inflection point in the company's history. Autonomous HCM is real, and it is with customers now. The engineering leader who takes this role will have the platform, the data, the team, and the mandate to build something that matters.

THE OPPORTUNITY
Organizations are navigating one of the most consequential workforce moments in a generation. AI is no longer a roadmap item; it is reshaping how companies manage their people, run their HR processes, and connect workforce decisions to business outcomes. SAP SuccessFactors is at the center of that shift.
We are looking for an engineering leader who can make Autonomous HCM, already real and in customers' hands, faster, stronger, and ready to scale globally. This is the role that builds the platform where AI connects every person, insight, and action, across the full HCM portfolio, for the world's largest organizations, in 160 countries.
You will report directly to the GM and Chief Product Officer of SAP SuccessFactors and partner closely with product, design, and go-to-market leadership to define and execute the engineering strategy. This is not a role for someone who wants to maintain the status quo. It is a role for someone who wants to lead a once-in-a-decade technology transition.

WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Manage engineering budgets and resource allocation with rigor, balancing sustaining investment, AI innovation, and product development
- Own the engineering strategy and execution for SAP SuccessFactors, including HR, talent, learning, workforce planning, employee experience, and the AI and agentic capabilities that run across all of them
- Lead and grow a world-class global engineering organization of 1,000+ engineers, building a culture of ownership, technical excellence, and relentless customer focus

The Business
Technology Workflows is the largest business at ServiceNow – and its core.  We build the products that run the technology estate— Service Management (Incident/Problem/Change), Operations Management (Discovery, Service Mapping, Event Management, etc.), the Configuration Management Database (CMDB), Asset Management, and Portfolio Management. Our customers use us to gain visibility of their technology estate, understand how it connects and performs, and act on it.
As AI moves from helping people work to acting on systems directly, the accuracy and reach of that picture becomes the limit on everything built above it. That puts the Technology Workflows business at the center of the company’s agentic strategy.
The Role
This is a senior individual contributor role and the strategy partner to the SVP of Technology Workflows and the General Managers and Product Leaders of each business unit.   You will not run a product line directly, nor will not have a team reporting directly to you.  Your work and impact come through the ability to partner and influence.  You will decide what this business should believe about where its market is going, be the key identifier of technological shifts and trends, and understand the current and future competitive landscape.  You will synthesize your findings with evidence and turn it into artifacts that help set long-term roadmap direction, budget allocations, staffing decisions, pricing, partnerships, and acquisitions.  You will interact with the ServiceNow Ventures team to help identify and assess sectors and individual companies for investment, with the Corporate Development team to create M&A chess boards and evaluate acquisition targets, and with the Corporate Strategy team to develop ServiceNow’s overall strategic posture.
Key to this role is a understanding of both business and deep technical constructs.  Technology Workflows is the most technical product group at ServiceNow and success in this role requires understanding how technical estates are run and the constantly changing stack used by practitioners.
If you want a defined product area and a team to build it, this is the wrong role. If you want to set the direction of a business at this scale without the machinery of owning it, few seats give you this much reach.

Position overview
The Head of AI/ML R&D decides, with evidence, whether an AI system works, how well, for whom, and at what cost. They come from data science and machine learning, and they build today with AI-native tools and agentic development.
The role owns the science of evaluation across every agent, the predictive and decision models behind the shared agents (churn, demand, payment recovery, fraud), and the experiment design that lets Finance count AI value once, against a holdout.

1. Evaluation science for every agent
o Set the enterprise eval methodology: golden-set design, sampling, labelling and inter-rater agreement, LLM-as-judge validation, slice analysis and statistical thresholds.
o Own the quality signals in the minimum telemetry contract: task success, groundedness, hallucination and escalation rates.
o Re-run evals per BU and tenant on every agent-core upgrade; catch regressions before customers do.

o Build and run the models the horizontal pods need: churn and retention uplift, payment-recovery propensity and timing, demand and capacity forecasting, later fraud and onboarding risk.
o Choose the right tool per task: classical ML, a small or fine-tuned model, retrieval, or a frontier LLM.
o Ship models to production on the golden path, with monitoring for drift and feedback loops.

o Drive cost per successful task down through distillation, caching strategy, smaller models and prompt and context optimization.

o Prototype varied techniques (agent memory, planning, multi-agent patterns, synthetic data) against real Xplor problems.

You own the asset portfolio.

The Opportunity
Adobe is seeking an exceptional Senior Director of Engineering to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of Growth Apps for Customer Experience Services (CES). In this high-impact role, you'll shape and scale the next generation of enterprise-grade AI applications—defining how our customers interact with intelligence-driven interfaces and workflows.

This is a unique opportunity for a seasoned engineering leader who thrives in a fast-paced, 0-to-1 product environment and is passionate about crafting intuitive, AI-powered user experiences at scale. You’ll collaborate across disciplines to bring bold ideas to life, continuously pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

What you’ll do
CES Growth Apps are Adobe’s scaled growth engine—turning customer experience intelligence, AI, and orchestration into repeatable systems that drive adoption, retention, and expansion at enterprise scale. They are a critical bridge between Adobe’s AI first product innovation and sustained customer and revenue outcomes.

Customer Experience Services (CES) Growth Apps represent the growth execution layer between Core platforms (Adobe Experience Platform, GenAI services, orchestration layers), Product led capabilities (Experience Cloud, GenStudio, AI driven workflows) and Go-to-market and Customer Success motions. They help ensure Adobe is not just shipping powerful products but is also systematically converting those products.  This leader will own the Engineering strategy for CES Growth Apps and partner closely with Product, Design, AI/ML to deliver deeply integrated, user-centric solutions that meet enterprise-grade standards.

The successful leader will:
- Foster a high-performing, inclusive, and creative engineering culture focused on iteration, design excellence, and technical rigor.
- Mentor and grow a world-class team of engineering leaders and ICs, attracting top talent and enabling career development at all levels.
- Serve as a visible thought leader both within Adobe and externally—representing the team at key industry events, conferences, and developer communities.
- Maintain a strong technical grasp of the team’s architecture and engineering decisions; be ready to dive deep and guide high-stakes decisions.

What you'll need to succeed
- 5+ years leading Engineering Directors and Senior Managers in a matrixed, high-growth environment.
- 15+ years of experience in software engineering, including significant leadership of teams building complex, AI-powered web applications at scale.
- Proven success delivering 0→1 product experiences, especially within AI, data platforms, or enterprise SaaS.
- Learning from launching Marketing agents, Ad tech or Sales tech products
- Demonstrated ability to drive user experience excellence through engineering, partnering effectively with product design and research teams.
- Strategic thinking with hands-on technical depth—you can articulate trade-offs, evaluate system architecture, and influence at all levels.

Company Description
HPS Investment Partners, a part of BlackRock, is a leading global, credit-focused alternative investment manager that seeks to provide creative capital solutions and generate attractive risk-adjusted returns for our clients. We manage various strategies across the capital structure, including privately negotiated senior debt; privately negotiated junior capital solutions in debt, preferred and equity formats; liquid credit including syndicated leveraged loans, collateralized loan obligations and high yield bonds; asset-based finance and real estate. The scale and breadth of our platform offers the flexibility to invest in companies large and small, through standard or customized solutions. At our core, we share a common thread of intellectual rigor and discipline that enables us to create value for our clients.

HPS was established in 2007 as a unit of Highbridge Capital Management, LLC (“HCM”), a subsidiary of JPMorgan Asset Management (“JPMAM”). On March 31, 2016, the senior executives of HPS acquired HPS and its subsidiaries from JPMAM and HCM (the “Transaction”. Following the Transaction, JPMAM retained a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently redeemed in April 2022. In June 2018, affiliates of Dyal Capital Partners made a passive minority investment in HPS. In February 2022, an affiliate of The Guardian Life Insurance Company of America made a passive minority investment in HPS, which was subsequently increased in August 2024. On July 1, 2025, BlackRock acquired the business and assets of HPS, with 100% of consideration paid in BlackRock equity (the “HPS/BlackRock Transaction”).

The HPS/BlackRock Transaction brings together BlackRock’s corporate and asset owner relationships with HPS’s diversified origination and capital flexibility. BlackRock and HPS have formed a new private financing solutions business unit (“PFS”) led by Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson, creating an integrated franchise with approximately $370 billion in client assets, including $205 billion of private credit assets. This combined platform, which has more than 590 investment professionals and approximately 1,300 employees globally, offers broad capabilities across senior and junior credit solutions, asset-based finance, real estate, CLOs and GP-LP solutions. As part of the HPS/BlackRock Transaction, Scott Kapnick, Scot French, and Michael Patterson have joined BlackRock’s Global Executive Committee, and Scott Kapnick has been appointed as an observer to the BlackRock Board

The GIP Infrastructure Credit platform invests across all major infrastructure markets and sectors, spanning the full capital structure and offering both investment grade and non-investment grade strategies. The team has deployed nearly c.$27bn across more than 270 investments globally. GIP's Infrastructure Debt business originates, structures and manages infrastructure investments designed to deliver attractive risk-adjusted returns with a focus on capital preservation and income generation.

This is an exciting opportunity for a highly motivated and experienced professional to join the Fund Finance team supporting GIP's Infrastructure Debt platform globally.

The successful candidate will play a central role in the operational and strategic management of the Global Infrastructure Debt ("GID") platform, GIP's flagship non-investment grade commingled fund platform, which invests across a broad range of infrastructure sectors and debt structures, including senior secured, second lien and holding company financings. Working closely with Investment Teams, Asset Management, Fund Accounting, Fund Administration, Legal, Tax, Portfolio Compliance and Investor Relations, the individual will help drive the effective management and continued growth of the platform.

The role spans the full investment lifecycle from transaction execution and portfolio construction through to liquidity management, valuations, financing oversight, reporting and investor servicing, while also supporting the continued evolution of the platform and launch of new products.

The successful candidate will have significant exposure to a broad range of structures including:
- Leveraged and unlevered commingled funds
- Rated note structures (vertical and horizontal)
- Asset-backed lending facilities
- Subscription and fund financing facilities
- Collateralized Fund Obligations (CFOs)
- Separately Managed Accounts (SMAs)
- Fund-of-One mandates
This is a highly visible role with regular interaction with senior management, investors, rating agencies, fund administrators and external counterparties.

Fund Oversight & Investment Execution

Staff Full-Stack Engineer (Director IC)

As a Staff Engineer at Capital One, you will be part of a community of technical experts working to define the future of banking in the cloud. You will work alongside our talented team of developers, machine learning experts, product managers and people leaders. Our Staff Engineers are leading experts in their domains, helping devise practical and reusable solutions to complex problems. You will drive innovation at multiple levels, helping optimize business outcomes while delivering strong technology solutions.

At Capital One, we believe diversity of thought strengthens our ability to influence, collaborate and provide the most innovative solutions across organizational boundaries. You will promote a culture of engineering excellence and strike the right balance between lending expertise and providing an inclusive environment where the ideas of others can be heard and championed. You will lead the way in creating next-generation talent for Capital One Tech, mentoring engineers and actively recruiting to keep building our community.

You will operate as a trusted advisor for our key technologies, platforms and capability domains, creating clear and concise communications, code samples, blog posts and other materials to share knowledge both inside and outside the organization. You will specialize in a particular subject area, but your input and impact will be sought and expected throughout the organization.

- Handle several projects simultaneously, balancing your time to maximize impact

- Collaborate with senior engineering and architecture leaders to define long-term platform strategy and API standards

workday:capital one:R1003189.description:
Staff Full-Stack Engineer (Director IC) - Digital Payments

As a Staff Engineer at Capital One, you will be part of a community of technical experts working to define the future of banking in the cloud. You will work alongside our talented team of developers, machine learning experts, product managers and people leaders. Our Staff Engineers are leading experts in their domains, helping devise practical and reusable solutions to complex problems. You will drive innovation at multiple levels, helping optimize business outcomes while delivering strong technology solutions.

At Capital One, we believe diversity of thought strengthens our ability to influence, collaborate and provide the most innovative solutions across organizational boundaries. You will promote a culture of engineering excellence and strike the right balance between lending expertise and providing an inclusive environment where the ideas of others can be heard and championed. You will lead the way in creating next-generation talent for Capital One Tech, mentoring engineers and actively recruiting to keep building our community.

Staff Engineers are expected to lead through technical contribution. You will operate as a trusted advisor for our key technologies, platforms and capability domains, creating clear and concise communications, code samples, blog posts and other materials to share knowledge both inside and outside the organization. You will specialize in a particular subject area, but your input and impact will be sought and expected throughout the organization.

The Global Payment Network (GPN) Digital Payments Technology organization designs, builds, and operates the mission-critical systems and infrastructure that seamlessly power complex money movement across domestic and international rails. We build and operate a high-volume, low-latency, and highly resilient distributed ecosystem that is simultaneously secure, performant, accurate, and nimble.  The Digital Payments team provides a tokenization platform that is critical in enabling secure commerce both online and with devices including ApplePay and GooglePay.  Digital Payments are a rapidly evolving space with constant innovation in how consumers pay.

This team operates with a startup mindset backed by enterprise scale. We are 100% cloud-native, deeply committed to engineering excellence, and aggressive in adopting cutting-edge AI tooling (including Claude Code, Windsurf, and custom AI agents) to dramatically accelerate our development lifecycle. You’ll be working hands-on with Senior Lead Engineers that are building the resilient, ultra-low-latency backbone of future global commerce.

What You’ll Do:
- Articulate and evangelize a bold technical vision for your domain
- Decompose complex problems into practical and operational solutions
- Ensure the quality of technical design and implementation
- Serve as an authoritative expert on non-functional system characteristics, such as performance, scalability and operability

- Monitor and use trends in risk exposure across markets and initiatives to inform ongoing international risk advisory and enhancement of ISE capabilities
- Lead, coach, and develop a team of risk professionals, growing their ability to operate independently across a complex, cross-functional stakeholder landscape

Data is at the center of everything we do. As a startup, we disrupted the credit card industry by individually personalizing every credit card offer using statistical modeling and the relational database, cutting edge technology in 1988! Who is NTE, NTE 35W, and LBJ?

The North Tarrant Express (NTE) was the first design-build-finance-operate-maintain managed lanes project in Texas and consisted of the complete reconstruction of 13.3 miles of the existing I-820/SH-183 corridor between Dallas and Fort Worth. Since opening in October 2014, nine months ahead of the contracted completion date, the general highway lanes are experiencing a 70% decrease in congestion time and a 15% increase in average speed. This Cintra-led project has doubled capacity and significantly improved mobility along this heavily congested corridor that traverses the heart of six cities through Northeast Tarrant County.

The North Tarrant Express 35W (NTE 35W) project spans 16.8 miles from I-30 in downtown Fort Worth to Eagle Parkway at the north end of Alliance Airport. The project is operated and maintained by the Cintra-led consortium in North Texas. This project has improved mobility by adding additional road capacity through a combination of general highway lanes and continuous frontage roads, along with tolled express lanes that use variable pricing to keep traffic moving.

The LBJ Express (LBJ) is currently the largest P3 operation in Texas and one of the largest ever undertaken in the U.S. It is a regionally-significant transportation improvement project in North Texas that is relieving severe congestion in the dense urban area of north Dallas. In 2009, the Cintra-led consortium was selected to complete the design, construction, finance, operation, and maintenance of the project along I-635 and I-35E. Since opening in September 2015, the general highway lanes are realizing a 60% decrease in congestion time and a 10% increase in average speed.

The Senior Director of Advancement Technology and Intelligence leads the data, technology, analytics, prospect development, gift administration, and operational infrastructure that powers DePauw University's Development and Alumni Engagement (DAE) program.

This position joins DePauw at a pivotal moment as the University selects and implements its next customer relationship management (CRM) platform. Interested candidates are invited to visit the Russell Reynolds Engage platform at Engage.RussellReynolds.com . Candidates will be asked to register and create a profile. From the home page, navigate to “Job Post”, click “Apply for Position”, and enter the following career code: 2609-162NA to submit materials for consideration. NOTE: Applying to the MacArthur career site may cause delays in review of your application.

The Opportunity
Philanthropy has long operated with fragmented data, duplicative processes, and systems that do not easily speak to one another. The Philanthropy Data Commons (PDC) was created to change that.

By enabling information to move securely across the systems that organizations already use, the PDC can reduce the repetitive administrative burden on nonprofits, help changemakers gain greater visibility to aligned funders, and give them greater control over how their information is shared, while giving funders a clearer view of organizations, needs, and funding flows.

The PDC has moved well beyond an idea. With significant foundational work completed, including a live Exchange application, an evolving governance framework, a growing network of funders and ecosystem participants, and more than 20 organizations committed to sharing data, PDC is entering an important period of transition and growth.

The focus now is on expanding participation, demonstrating the value of shared data at greater scale, and building the coalition that can make PDC an enduring part of how philanthropy works.

The inaugural Executive Director will have a rare chance to help shape the next stage of the initiative and a broader shift in the field. They will build on significant investment and momentum while helping the PDC grow its reach, deepen its partnerships, strengthen its financial sustainability, and establish its long-term organizational home.

At a time when advances in AI are making access to trusted, well-governed data increasingly important, the PDC has the potential to become essential infrastructure for a more connected, informed, and effective philanthropic sector. For an entrepreneurial leader energized by building in ambiguity, this is a chance to take years of investment and a powerful sector-wide idea and turn it into something enduring, shaping not only the future of the PDC but how philanthropy shares and uses data.

About the Philanthropy Data Commons
Conceptualized in 2021, the Philanthropy Data Commons is a collaborative initiative temporarily hosted by Mac Services, Inc. that connects the systems, organizations, and data that philanthropy runs on. It provides a shared infrastructure that allows funders, changemakers, and the ecosystem partners they already use to share information on their own terms.

‎
The Director, Risk Adjustment Product & Technology will lead the product roadmap, and technology capabilities that enable Mosaic Health to identify, prioritize, orchestrate, and capture burden-of-illness opportunities across its patient populations.

This role will own the evolution of Mosaic’s enterprise Burden of Illness (BOI) Hub—the centralized intelligence and orchestration layer that brings together clinical, claims, payer, attribution, and supplemental data to determine which patients and clinical opportunities should be acted upon, through which intervention, and at what point in the workflow.

The Director will move the organization from fragmented, vendor-specific, and manually driven prioritization toward an enterprise-owned approach to risk adjustment decisioning and orchestration. - Own the product vision, strategy, roadmap, and operating model for Mosaic’s enterprise risk adjustment technology capabilities.
- Lead development and maturation of the Burden of Illness Hub as the central orchestration capability for risk adjustment and related clinical opportunities.
- Translate Risk Adjustment, Clinical, Operations, market, payer, and financial requirements into scalable product and technology capabilities.
- Establish a clear distinction between:
- enterprise-owned decisioning and prioritization,
- foundational data capabilities,
- execution engines,
- vendor functionality, and
- provider, coder, and operational workflows.
- Define the target-state architecture and multi-year roadmap for moving from fragmented tools and processes to a standardized enterprise platform.

- Build the Hub as the enterprise system for:
- patient eligibility and prioritization,

- suspect and opportunity aggregation,
- opportunity deduplication,

- intervention routing,
- opportunity status and disposition,
- attribution and retention interventions, and
- enterprise performance analytics.

The Engineering Director will report to the Propulsion Systems Business Unit General Manager, with accountability for business unit level engineering strategy, technical leadership, technology innovation, core processes, and workforce planning.

The Director will lead a multi-disciplined engineering team dedicated to executing current and future programs as well as developing next generation propulsion technologies. - Bachelor’s degree in an Engineering discipline, such as Mechanical, Electrical, Systems, or Software; Master’s degree in Engineering or MBA preferred.

NFR is part of the Second Line of Defense providing independent oversight and challenge to management across compliance and operational risks. The Vice President, Digital Product Strategy leads Nexstar’s digital product strategy and owns the product initiatives behind two pillars of the 2027 digital strategy: deepening audience relationships and modernizing our platforms. The role turns that work into a sequenced roadmap, clear targets, and shipped products across The Hill, NewsNation, and Nexstar’s local stations, and supports strategic projects, from new business opportunities to partnership and investment evaluations. The VP also plays a critical role in shaping and managing Nexstar’s corporate digital strategy, from annual and quarterly priorities down to product roadmaps.

Two flagship initiatives anchor the role in 2027. The first is Nexstar’s first-party data strategy: growing known, registered users across the portfolio and building the data capture and identity infrastructure behind them. The second is Mobile App 2.0: the redesign, build, and rollout of Nexstar’s station mobile app experience, starting in a lead test market and scaling across the station footprint.

The VP holds direct ownership and day-to-day decision authority over the initiatives, roadmaps, and team she leads, and is accountable for keeping editorial, marketing, revenue, and product aligned behind them.
Success in this role will require strong matrix leadership: the ability to build trusted relationships, create alignment, and form durable alliances across teams whose resources do not directly report into the role. The VP will need to influence and marshal shared engineering, design, product, editorial, marketing, revenue, and station leadership capacity behind the highest-priority initiatives, ensuring that complex cross-functional work moves from strategy to execution with clear ownership and momentum.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

2027 Priorities

• First-Party Data (Deepen Audience Relationships): Owns first-party data strategy across the portfolio, including free account registration, profile data collection, identity resolution, and known-user growth. Sets and owns known-user targets, and defines the roadmap for data capture and identity infrastructure that underpins marketing, advertising, and subscription use cases.
• Mobile App 2.0 (Modernize Our Platforms): Leads the design, development, and rollout of the next-generation Nexstar station mobile app, from a lead test market to the full station footprint.
Owns the product vision, vendor and partner management, launch sequencing, and adoption and engagement targets, and makes the app a primary engine for registration and first-party data.
• OVP Upgrade (Modernize Our Platforms): Supports, but does not own, the upgrade of Nexstar’s online video platform (OVP), the other major platform modernization effort in 2027. Contributes product input where it intersects with Mobile App 2.0 and first-party data.
• CTV (Modernize Our Platforms): Helps drive the enhancement of Nexstar’s connected TV (CTV) presence, improving the viewer experience across Nexstar’s CTV apps

The Director of IT Business Operations is a senior leadership role responsible for driving the strategic and financial efficiency of IT functions within the Office of the CIO. Overview
RAND is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research organization that provides leaders with the information they need to make evidence-based decisions. In pursuing this mission, RAND helps sponsors at the highest levels of U.S. national and homeland security and in related roles throughout the U.S. government with their toughest problems. This requires the ability to conduct work at all levels of classification while using cutting-edge computing and analytic capabilities, and it requires RAND to remain a close and trusted partner with these officials and agencies by upholding the highest standards of security. To accomplish this, the S&CO organization works in partnership with RAND’s research divisions, Information Services (IS), and Workplace Services to ensure we have top-notch classified research capabilities and security processes that enable researchers to conduct their work effectively, efficiently, and responsibly, while maintaining uncompromising security.

As a member of RAND’s senior leadership team, reporting to the senior vice president, chief financial and operating officer, the executive director leads the 55-person S&CO organization and serves as RAND’s Chief Security Officer. The executive director will develop and provide classified research capabilities that enable researchers in RAND’s Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs) and other research divisions to execute cutting-edge, complex research responsive to the top priorities of U.S. national and homeland security. Over the last few years, S&CO has significantly upgraded RAND’s classified capabilities, and its culture has been shifting from a compliance orientation to a mission-focused partnership with researchers. - Experience shipping enterprise security or identity products at scale.
- A track record of driving alignment across multiple teams without direct authority.
- Exposure to AI agent security, non-human identity, or API and gateway enforcement is a strong plus.
- Excellent written and verbal communication, and the ability to explain complex architecture to executives, customers, and engineers alike.

Success looks like
- A single, well-understood authorization architecture adopted across the product teams.

Who we are looking for
The Head of Enterprise Architecture owns the target-state design of the technology estate and the standards, patterns and governance through which it is realised . This is the architectural blueprint that determines how every platform, application and integration in the firm is built, connected, secured and retired.

The mandate is to reduce complexity while increasing optionality — cutting technical debt, rationalising a fragmented estate, and establishing the reusable architectural foundations that let engineering teams move faster within known-good boundaries. Success is measured not in documents published but in estate outcomes: fewer bespoke solutions, faster architectural decisions, demonstrably lower run cost, and an architecture capable of absorbing the pace of change that Frontier AI and post-quantum cryptography will impose.

A central element of this mandate is establishing the architecture that makes the firm AI-forward — the compute, serving, integration and control foundations on which AI becomes a governed production capability rather than a portfolio of experiments. This is delivered in deliberate partnership with the Head of Data & AI, who owns model strategy, data products and AI delivery.

This is a deeply technical leadership role . The successful candidate is a credible principal-level architect who has personally designed systems at scale, and who will lead through technical authority rather than positional mandate — equally effective authoring a reference architecture, defending a standard to a skeptical business-unit CIO, and presenting an estate rationalization case to the Senior Leadership.

Why this role is Important to us
- Architecture is an enabling layer, not a gate. Governance exists to accelerate good decisions, not to inspect bad ones after the fact. If review is the bottleneck, the pattern library has failed.
- Patterns over permissions. The fastest, cheapest, pre-approved way to build is to use an existing pattern. Teams may deviate through a time-boxed, registered exception — and inherit the support and compliance burden of doing so.
- Reduce before you add. Every new pattern admitted to the library should retire something. Complexity is the primary long-term cost driver of the estate.
- Serve the whole estate. Mainframe, vendor-package, analytics and quant populations receive proportionate patterns and standards. An architecture that governs only greenfield services has failed.
- Cost is an architectural property. Spend, unit economics and run cost are designed in, not discovered in the invoice — including the economics of accelerated compute and inference.
- Complementary, not overlapping. Where a peer function owns a domain — Data & AI, Cyber, Developer Platforms — EA owns the interfaces, standards and cross-domain coherence, not the delivery.

You'll lead engineering on a multi-year programme to modernize and migrate a large portfolio of middle-office applications to AWS. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. As one of the first schools of social work in the United States, the Crown Family School of Social Work, Policy, and Practice has shaped the field for more than 100 years. Azure is now the home of World Finance's core business systems, and the company will keep building there. The Director of IT Cloud Operations owns the Azure platform as a managed program: setting the strategy, designing the target architecture, and leading the execution that moves the environment from one built one resource at a time to a governed, secure-by-default cloud. The Director leads a small, high-leverage team, draws on the wider IT organization and external delivery partners, and is accountable for where the cloud is headed and how well it runs along the way.
This is a player-coach seat. In a given week the Director may set the quarter's roadmap with IT leadership, review a landing-zone design and a pipeline change from the team, pair on an infrastructure-as-code module, work through a remediation plan with Information Security, and manage an external partner's delivery. Establish a scored maturity model with a named owner for each capability, reassess at least annually, and use the gaps to shape the platform roadmap and report progress to IT leadership.
- Own the environment cleanup already underway: retire orphaned and idle resources, close platform-level exposures, and turn point-in-time findings into a routed, SLA-backed remediation flow.

- Run cloud spend as a managed number through tagging, right-sizing, reservations, lifecycle controls, and reporting.
- Establish prioritization, documentation, review gates, and audit evidence supporting SOX ITGC, GLBA/FTC Safeguards, and PCI DSS.
- Ensure monitoring, backup standards, logging, and remediation of platform-level posture findings.
- Other duties as assigned.
